analysis.executiveSummary: Ravens Regime proposes trading Jaylen Waddle, Deebo Samuel Sr., and Kyle Monangai to Mile High Royal Lions for Garrett Wilson and Travis Kelce. From Ravens Regime's perspective as a Win Championship contender, this acquisition delivers a massive starting lineup boost by replacing Eli Raridon (21.9 C-AVI) with Travis Kelce (79.3 C-AVI) at TE and slotting Garrett Wilson (76.8 C-AVI) into WR2. However, for Mile High Royal Lions—whose goal is also set to Win Championship—surrendering two locked-in cornerstone starters for secondary depth assets creates a severe -52.6 C-AVI drop in their starting lineup. Because Mile High will reject this 3-for-2 depth offer, AVI recommends revising the proposal by adding Ravens Regime's 2029 1st Round pick to make the transaction strategically viable for both franchises.

submitted.summary: The submitted construction heavily favors Ravens Regime (+80.2 C-AVI starting lineup surge) while severely crippling Mile High Royal Lions (-52.6 C-AVI starting lineup drop). Surrendering two elite starters forces Mile High to downgrade TE1 to Dalton Schultz and WR2 to Jaylen Waddle, conflicting directly with their Win Championship objective.

officialAviAnalysis.sideAChampionshipImpact: Extremely positive (+80.2 starting C-AVI). Solving the TE hole with Travis Kelce (+57.4 C-AVI over Eli Raridon) and adding Garrett Wilson (76.8 C-AVI) gives Ravens Regime a dominant title-contending starting eight.
officialAviAnalysis.sideADynastyImpact: Net negative (-60.8 D-AVI). Trading away Jaylen Waddle (84.0 D-AVI), Deebo Samuel Sr. (69.2 D-AVI), and Kyle Monangai (78.7 D-AVI) for Travis Kelce (79.7 D-AVI) and Garrett Wilson (91.4 D-AVI) sacrifices multi-year depth volume.
officialAviAnalysis.sideARosterImpact: Consolidates depth into two high-end starters, shifting KC Concepcion Jr. and Carnell Tate into primary FLEX positions.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBChampionshipImpact: Severely negative (-52.6 starting C-AVI). Forces Mile High Royal Lions to start Dalton Schultz (51.5 C-AVI) at TE and Jaylen Waddle (54.0 C-AVI) at WR2.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBDynastyImpact: Net positive (+60.8 D-AVI). Replaces 37-year-old Kelce with younger multi-year pieces across WR and RB.
officialAviAnalysis.sideBRosterImpact: Adds backfield depth with Monangai behind Gibbs/Coleman and WR depth with Waddle/Deebo, but leaves TE vulnerable.
officialAviAnalysis.valueAssessment: While total C-AVI exchanged is relatively close (141.9 sent vs 156.1 received), the starting lineup impact is heavily skewed toward Ravens Regime.

publicMarketAnalysis.summary: Public dynasty consensus ranks Garrett Wilson as an elite top-12 dynasty WR1 (age 26) with long-term cornerstone value, while Travis Kelce remains a high-end redraft TE1 despite age 37 retirement concerns.
publicMarketAnalysis.aviVsMarket: AVI aligns with market consensus on Wilson's top-tier dynasty rank (91.4 D-AVI) and captures Kelce's elite win-now utility (79.3 C-AVI) relative to his shorter dynasty horizon (79.7 D-AVI).
relevantContext: Garrett Wilson is reportedly expected to return in Week 10 from a concussion, maintaining his high-volume WR baseline.
Travis Kelce leads the Chiefs in receiving targets and yards, remaining a locked-in weekly TE1.
Jaylen Waddle and Deebo Samuel Sr. represent solid WR2/FLEX assets but lack Wilson's elite target ceiling.
Kyle Monangai provides solid young RB depth in Chicago's backfield.
